## Per case, old vs new
### S1-01
- Title: unchanged: A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z
- Old preconditions:
  - Scenario: Your shop has four customers with open invoices whose names start alike and differ only by a number, a dash or capitals.
  - You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location. [For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.]
  - Four customers have open invoices on today's date: {Customer-A}, {Customer-B}, {Customer-C} and {Customer-D}. Their names start with the same word and then differ by a number, a dash or capitals, as in the example. [For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-01 10 Trucking, {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-01 2 Trucking, {Customer-C} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-01 A-1 Towing, {Customer-D} is ZZAUTOTEST S1-01 a1 towing.]
  - Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  - If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
- New preconditions:
  - Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  - Have four customers with open invoices on today's date, named "10 Trucking" (customer A), "2 Trucking" (customer B), "A-1 Towing" (customer C) and "a1 towing" (customer D). Their names differ by a number, a dash or capitals.
  - Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  - Open A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  - If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
- Steps: unchanged wording
- New steps: 1. Look at the header of the customer name column (the first column). | 2. Without clicking any column header, find the four customers in the list (scroll down until they load if they are further down).
- Old results: Step 1: the customer name column (the first column) is marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading). | Step 2: all four customers are listed, reading from top to bottom {Customer-A}, then {Customer-B}, then {Customer-C}, then {Customer-D} (other customers may sit between them). With the example names: "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" because names compare character by character, and "A-1 Towing" comes before "a1 towing" because capitals are ignored and the dash compares as a character.
- New results:
  - Step 1: The customer name column (the first column) is marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).
  - Step 2: All four customers are listed, reading from top to bottom customer A, then customer B, then customer C, then customer D (other customers may sit between them). / "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" because names compare character by character. / "A-1 Towing" comes before "a1 towing" because capitals are ignored and the dash compares as a character.

### S2-39
- Title: unchanged: A/R Collection: a column where every row is the same does not reorder
- Old preconditions:
  - Scenario: Your shop works at two locations, and one customer has three overdue invoices, all at the same location.
  - You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location. [For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.]
  - The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order. [For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.]
  - Customer {Customer-A} has three overdue invoices on today's date, {Invoice-A}, {Invoice-B} and {Invoice-C}, all at {Location-A}; in number order they read A, B, C. [For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-39 Same Place; {Invoice-A} is S1-99, {Invoice-B} S1-100 and {Invoice-C} S1-101.]
  - Starting screen: A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  - If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
- New preconditions:
  - Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role), with location A as your current location.
  - Have open documents in these reports at two locations, location A and your other location.
  - Make sure you are enrolled at both locations.
  - Have a customer, customer A, with three overdue invoices on today's date, invoice A, invoice B and invoice C, all at location A; in number order they read A, B, C.
  - Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  - Open A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  - If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
- Old steps: 1. Expand {Customer-A}'s group. | 2. Click the "Location" header.
- New steps: 1. Expand customer A's group. | 2. Click the "Location" header.
- Old results: Step 1: the group shows the three invoices, each with Location {Location-A}. | Step 2: the Location column is marked as sorted, but nothing visibly moves inside the group: every row has the same value, and the three invoices stay ordered by number: {Invoice-A}, {Invoice-B}, {Invoice-C}.
- New results:
  - Step 1: The group shows the three invoices, each with Location A.
  - Step 2: The Location column is marked as sorted, but nothing visibly moves inside the group: every row has the same value. / The three invoices stay ordered by number: invoice A, invoice B, invoice C.

### S2-40
- Title: unchanged: A/R Detail: column headings are in Title Case on screen, PDF and CSV
- Old preconditions:
  - Scenario: Your shop works at two locations with open customer documents, and you check the A/R Detail column headings on screen and in exports.
  - You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location. [For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.]
  - The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order. [For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.]
  - The report has open documents at both locations on today's date.
  - Starting screen: A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with every group expanded (Expand all).
  - If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
- New preconditions:
  - Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  - Have open documents in these reports at two locations, so the Location column shows.
  - Make sure the report has open documents at both locations on today's date.
  - Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  - Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  - Leave the report with every group expanded (Expand all).
  - If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
- Steps: unchanged wording
- New steps: 1. Read the column headings, letter for letter, capitals included. | 2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu. | 3. Open the PDF and read its column headings. | 4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu. | 5. Open the CSV in a plain text editor and read its column heading row.
- Old results: Step 1: "Date", "Location", "Transaction Type", "ID", "Customer Full Name", "Due Date", "Amount", "Open Balance" (the chevron button sits before "Date"): every word starts with a capital letter, as on the A/P reports. | Step 2: the PDF downloads. | Step 3: the PDF's column headings read exactly as on screen, capitals included. | Step 4: the CSV downloads. | Step 5: the heading row (right after the "As of: " and "Locations: All locations" rows) holds the same headings, letter for letter as on screen, and an "Aging Bucket" column for the bucket name ("Customer Full Name" is already among the headings).
- New results:
  - Step 1: "Date", "Location", "Transaction Type", "ID", "Customer Full Name", "Due Date", "Amount", "Open Balance" (the chevron button sits before "Date"): every word starts with a capital letter, as on the A/P reports.
  - Step 2: The PDF downloads.
  - Step 3: The PDF's column headings read exactly as on screen, capitals included.
  - Step 4: The CSV downloads.
  - Step 5: The heading row (right after the "As of: " and "Locations: All locations" rows) holds the same headings, letter for letter as on screen, and an "Aging Bucket" column for the bucket name ("Customer Full Name" is already among the headings).

### S4-09
- Title: unchanged: A/R Detail: the group row stays pinned under the headings
- Old preconditions:
  - Scenario: Two neighbouring aging buckets on A/R Detail each hold more lines than fit on the screen, and you scroll down.
  - You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location. [For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.]
  - On today's date the report has two buckets, {Bucket-A} and the next bucket below it, {Bucket-B}, each with more lines than fit on the screen. [For example: {Bucket-A} is "31-60 days past due" and {Bucket-B} is "1-30 days past due".]
  - Starting screen: A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with the groups of {Bucket-A} and {Bucket-B} expanded.
  - If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
- New preconditions:
  - Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  - Make sure that on today's date the report has two buckets, bucket A and the next bucket below it, bucket B, each with more lines than fit on the screen.
  - Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  - Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  - Leave the report with the groups of bucket A and bucket B expanded.
  - If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
- Old steps: 1. Scroll down slowly into {Bucket-A}'s rows. | 2. Keep scrolling until {Bucket-B}'s row reaches the top. | 3. Keep scrolling into {Bucket-B}'s rows. | 4. Scroll back up slowly until you are inside {Bucket-A}'s rows again. | 5. Scroll down fast through {Bucket-A}'s and {Bucket-B}'s rows. | 6. Scroll fast back up through {Bucket-B}'s and {Bucket-A}'s rows.
- New steps: 1. Scroll down slowly into bucket A's rows. | 2. Keep scrolling until bucket B's row reaches the top. | 3. Keep scrolling into bucket B's rows. | 4. Scroll back up slowly until you are inside bucket A's rows again. | 5. Scroll down fast through bucket A's and bucket B's rows. | 6. Scroll fast back up through bucket B's and bucket A's rows.
- Old results: Step 1: {Bucket-A}'s row stays pinned just under the column headings while its rows scroll beneath it; it shows the bucket's chevron (pointing down) and its label: the bucket's name and count; it shows no amounts (the bucket's sums stay in its own subtotal row). | Step 2: {Bucket-B}'s row pushes {Bucket-A}'s row up and off and takes its place; only one group row is pinned at a time. | Step 3: {Bucket-B}'s row stays pinned. | Step 4: the change reverses: {Bucket-A}'s row comes back down into the pinned place. | Step 5: at speed too, each pinned row is pushed up and replaced cleanly: it never covers the column headings or the Totals row at the bottom, and two group rows never overlap. | Step 6: the same going back up: each pinned row is replaced cleanly, never covers the column headings or the Totals row, and two group rows never overlap.
- New results:
  - Step 1: Bucket A's row stays pinned just under the column headings while its rows scroll beneath it. / It shows the bucket's chevron (pointing down) and its label: the bucket's name and count. / It shows no amounts (the bucket's sums stay in its own subtotal row).
  - Step 2: Bucket B's row pushes bucket A's row up and off and takes its place. / Only one group row is pinned at a time.
  - Step 3: Bucket B's row stays pinned.
  - Step 4: The change reverses: bucket A's row comes back down into the pinned place.
  - Step 5: At speed too, each pinned row is pushed up and replaced cleanly: it never covers the column headings or the Totals row at the bottom. / Two group rows never overlap.
  - Step 6: The same going back up: each pinned row is replaced cleanly, never covers the column headings or the Totals row. / Two group rows never overlap.

  - Step 4: The change reverses: vendor A's row comes back down into the pinned place.
  - Step 5: At speed too, each pinned row is pushed up and replaced cleanly: it never covers the column headings or the Totals row at the bottom. / Two group rows never overlap.

### D-29
- Title: unchanged: Design: A/R Location chip and menu match Sales By Customer's
- Old preconditions:
  - Scenario: Your shop works at two locations, and you compare the A/R Location filter with the one on Sales By Customer.
  - You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location. [For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.]
  - The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order. [For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.]
  - Starting screen: A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom.
  - Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) is open in a second tab of the same window, for comparison.
  - If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
- New preconditions:
  - Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  - Have open documents in these reports at two locations, so the Location menu lists two locations ("2 selected").
  - Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, in light theme at 100% zoom.
  - Open A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu).
  - Open Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) in a second tab of the same window, for comparison.
  - If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
- Steps: unchanged wording
- New steps: 1. Look at the Location chip and compare with Sales By Customer's. | 2. Click it and read the menu, row by row, letter for letter. | 3. Compare the open menu with Sales By Customer's open Location menu. | 4. Switch ShopView to dark theme. | 5. Click the Location chip again.
- Old results: Step 1: label "Location" with the location pin icon, the same chip as Sales By Customer's. | Step 2: in this order: "Select all", the count ("2 selected"), the locations with the ticked ones first, and "Clear selection"; no search box (fewer than 9 locations). | Step 3: the same menu: same rows, order, tick boxes, spacing and position under the chip. | Step 4: the page switches to dark theme. | Step 5: the menu opens: the same, readable in dark theme, nothing clipped.

  - Step 1: Label "Location" with the location pin icon, the same chip as Sales By Customer's.
  - Step 2: In this order: "Select all", the count ("2 selected"), the locations with the ticked ones first, and "Clear selection". / No search box (fewer than 9 locations).
  - Step 3: The same menu: same rows, order, tick boxes, spacing and position under the chip.
  - Step 4: The page switches to dark theme.
  - Step 5: The menu opens: the same, readable in dark theme, nothing clipped.
